source.title: Global Bidirectional Power Converter for EV Charger Market to Reach USD 170.07 Million by 2034, Driven by Vehicle-to-Grid Technology and EV Charging Innovation
source.body:
PUNE, India, November 23, 2026 – The global bidirectional power converter for EV charger market is projected to reach USD 170.07 million by 2034, registering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 23.8% during 2026–2034, according to a new report published by EnergyResourcesInsights. The market was valued at USD 24.93 million in 2025 and is estimated to reach USD 30.86 million in 2026.
The report, titled “Bidirectional Power Converter for EV Charger Market – Size, Share & Industry Analysis, By Conversion Stage, By Power Class, By Device Technology, By End Use, and Global Forecast, 2026–2034,” examines charger-side power-conversion equipment that enables electricity to flow in both directions between electric vehicles and connected electrical systems.
Bidirectional power converters are essential components in vehicle-to-grid (V2G), vehicle-to-home (V2H) and vehicle-to-building (V2B) applications. Unlike conventional charging systems that transfer electricity in only one direction, bidirectional converters allow controlled energy transfer from the grid to the vehicle battery and, when supported by the vehicle and installation, back toward a building or electrical network.
The growing adoption of electric vehicles, increasing interest in distributed energy resources, renewable energy integration and demand for flexible electricity management are creating opportunities for bidirectional charging technologies. However, commercial deployment depends on vehicle compatibility, grid-export permissions, charging infrastructure standards and the economics of reverse energy transfer.
Bidirectional Power Converter for EV Charger Market at a Glance
•	2025 Market Size: USD 24.93 Million
•	2026 Market Estimate: USD 30.86 Million
•	2034 Market Forecast: USD 170.07 Million
•	CAGR (2026–2034): 23.8%
•	Largest Regional Market: Asia-Pacific
•	Report ID: #391
•	Report Length: 96 Pages
•	Publication: November 2026
Key Factors Driving the Bidirectional Power Converter for EV Charger Market
1. Growing Demand for Vehicle-to-Grid and Building Energy Exchange
The development of vehicle-to-grid and vehicle-to-building applications is creating demand for power converters capable of supporting reverse electricity transfer. Bidirectional charging can enable compatible electric vehicles to provide energy to buildings or support grid-connected energy management. Fleet operators and commercial facilities are potential early adopters where vehicle schedules and electricity tariffs support controlled energy exchange.
2. Increasing Adoption of Bidirectional EV Charging Platforms
Charging-equipment manufacturers are incorporating reverse-flow functionality into selected charger designs. Bidirectional AC/DC front ends and isolated DC/DC conversion stages allow power to move between the electrical grid and vehicle batteries under controlled operating conditions. The expansion of compatible charging platforms is expected to support demand for specialized converter modules.
3. Growing Adoption of Silicon-Carbide Power Electronics
Silicon-carbide (SiC) semiconductor technology is gaining importance in high-voltage power-conversion applications. SiC-based converter designs can support higher switching frequencies and compact power-stage architectures. Manufacturers are focusing on efficiency, thermal performance, voltage coverage and power density to improve bidirectional charger designs.
4. Expansion of Grid-Interactive Charging Infrastructure
The growing integration of renewable electricity, distributed energy resources and electric vehicles is increasing interest in grid-interactive charging systems. Bidirectional converters can support controlled power transfer and local energy management, provided the surrounding charging system meets relevant grid and safety requirements.
5. Increasing Demand for Standardized and Modular Converter Systems
Charging-equipment manufacturers are seeking modular power-conversion platforms that can be integrated into different charger configurations. Standardized converter blocks can reduce engineering complexity and support scalable charging-system designs. Reliability, parallel operation, protection features and technical support remain important purchasing considerations.
Market Segmentation
The Bidirectional Power Converter for EV Charger Market is segmented across four major categories:
•	By Conversion Stage: Bidirectional AC/DC Front End, Isolated Bidirectional DC/DC, Combined Multi-Stage Modules.
•	By Power Class: Up to 11 kW, Above 11 kW to 30 kW, Above 30 kW.
•	By Device Technology: Silicon Carbide, Silicon MOSFET/IGBT, Gallium Nitride.
•	By End Use: Public and Workplace DC Charging, Home/Building V2X Charging, Fleet and Depot Energy Exchange.
Bidirectional AC/DC front-end converters accounted for an estimated 46% of 2025 market revenue, making them the leading conversion-stage category. The above-11-kW-to-30-kW power class represented an estimated 49% share, reflecting demand for medium-power converter modules used in commercial charging applications.
Silicon-carbide-based power stages accounted for an estimated 55% of market revenue, supported by their relevance to high-voltage switching and compact power-conversion architectures. Public and workplace DC charging represented an estimated 44% of revenue by end use.
These segment shares are analytical estimates presented in the report and relate specifically to charger-side converter-stage revenue, rather than complete EV charging station sales.
Regional Outlook
Asia-Pacific is the largest regional market, accounting for an estimated 57% of global revenue in 2025. The region benefits from established power-electronics manufacturing, EV charging equipment production and growing interest in bidirectional energy-transfer applications. China is a major manufacturing and product-development centre, while Japan and South Korea contribute power semiconductor expertise and vehicle-to-building technology development.
Europe represents the second-largest regional market, with an estimated 22% share of 2025 revenue. Demand is supported by grid-interactive charging development, renewable energy self-consumption and vehicle-to-grid applications. Germany, France, the Netherlands and Nordic markets offer opportunities through commercial properties, fleet charging hubs and renewable-energy installations. Grid-interconnection requirements and vehicle compatibility remain important adoption considerations.
North America is an emerging market for bidirectional EV charger converters, particularly through vehicle-to-home applications, backup power and fleet energy management. The United States and Canada are exploring opportunities to use compatible electric vehicles as flexible energy resources for homes, commercial buildings and selected facilities. Utility requirements, vehicle interoperability and installation standards influence market development.
South America represents an earlier-stage market, with opportunities associated with commercial fleet electrification, renewable-energy integration and distributed power applications. Brazil, Chile and Colombia offer potential development opportunities, although electricity tariffs, imported equipment costs and grid-export permissions influence adoption.
The Middle East & Africa market is developing through selected EV fleet, commercial property and solar-linked charging applications. Bidirectional converter opportunities may emerge in logistics facilities, private microgrids and commercial buildings. High ambient temperatures, dust, grid conditions, technical support and export authorization are important equipment and project considerations.
Regional market shares are estimates of charger-side converter-stage sales rather than independently published regional revenue series.
Competitive Landscape
The global bidirectional power converter for EV charger market includes specialist power-module manufacturers and semiconductor technology providers supporting converter development and qualification.
Key companies covered in the report include:
•	UUGreenPower
•	Infypower
•	Texas Instruments
•	STMicroelectronics
UUGreenPower and Infypower publish bidirectional power-module and converter product offerings relevant to charger-side applications. Texas Instruments and STMicroelectronics provide semiconductor technologies, reference designs and engineering platforms that support the development of bidirectional charging architectures.
Competition is primarily based on conversion efficiency, supported DC voltage range, power density, thermal management, reverse-power-transfer capability, protection functions and integration flexibility. Manufacturers are also focusing on reliable parallel operation, standardized converter modules, product qualification and technical support.
The report distinguishes commercial converter-module suppliers from semiconductor and engineering-platform providers. Reference designs and evaluation platforms demonstrate technical architectures but should not be interpreted as evidence of commercial module shipment volumes.
